sections.1:
Archlin is a specialty chemicals manufacturing business headquartered in Georgia, USA, operating on SAP S/4HANA with a current Excel-based planning process. Archlin’s planning maturity is partially automated and characterized by siloed systems, with no centralized planning platform across North America and Europe. The current demand planning process requires demand planners to spend significant time consolidating forecasts from multiple regions, and manual Excel activities are causing delays in monthly planning cycles. Forecast accuracy is approximately 68%, and inventory levels are higher than target due to poor forecast visibility, making poor inventory planning a key business pain point for Archlin.

Archlin’s planned solution direction is the implementation of Kinaxis RapidResponse for Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Optimization, with Phase 1 focused on Demand Planning. The Demand Planning scope is intended to establish statistical baseline forecast generation, enable planner forecast overrides, track forecast history and changes, and support multiple forecast hierarchies. The solution is also expected to improve collaboration by allowing sales teams to provide forecast input, enabling approval workflows, and providing forecast comparison reports. Analytics capabilities in scope include measuring forecast accuracy, measuring forecast bias, tracking MAPE by product family, and providing dashboard-based reporting.

The implementation will need to address the data and integration foundation required to support Archlin’s planning processes. Required interfaces identified for the solution include Product Master, Customer Master, Sales Orders, Inventory Balances, Purchase Orders, and Production Orders, with a data refresh frequency of every 4 hours. Business users emphasized the need for collaborative forecasting and visibility across regions, while demand planners requested automated forecast generation with the ability to manually override forecasts when market conditions change. Supply planners highlighted recurring raw material shortage issues and requested exception-based alerts, which aligns to the broader planning transformation objective beyond the Phase 1 Demand Planning focus.

Archlin’s expected business outcomes include improved forecast accuracy, reduced inventory, shorter planning cycles, improved planner productivity, and a single source of planning data. The documented success criteria include Forecast Accuracy greater than 85%, Inventory Reduction greater than 15%, Planning Cycle Reduction greater than 30%, Improved Planner Productivity, and Single Source of Planning Data. Leadership expects measurable improvements in forecast accuracy and inventory reduction within six months of go-live, making the Phase 1 Demand Planning implementation a foundational step in Archlin’s broader planning transformation.

Archlin business users have emphasized the need for collaborative forecasting and improved visibility across regions, with better coordination between sales, operations, and supply chain teams.

The required collaboration capabilities include enabling sales teams to provide forecast input, supporting approval workflows, and providing forecast comparison reports. The analytics scope includes measuring forecast accuracy, measuring forecast bias, tracking MAPE by product family, and providing dashboard-based reporting.

The implementation will require integration of key planning inputs and transactional data from Archlin’s SAP S/4HANA environment and related source processes. Required interfaces include Product Master, Customer Master, Sales Orders, Inventory Balances, Purchase Orders, and Production Orders, with a required data refresh frequency of every 4 hours. These integrations are intended to support a single source of planning data and improve the timeliness and reliability of demand planning outputs. Demand planners have specifically requested automated forecast generation with the ability to manually override forecasts when market conditions change, while business stakeholders have highlighted collaborative forecasting and cross-region visibility as central priorities.
